summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (EF 20%), atrial fibrillation, restrictive lung disease, chronic kidney disease, and a prior lung nodule treated with Cyberknife radiation was admitted for orthopnea and worsening shortness of breath when lying flat. Evaluation revealed no acute cardiac decompensation, with stable BNP and no pulmonary edema on imaging. His symptoms were attributed to mixed obstructive and restrictive lung disease, possibly exacerbated by amiodarone use and underlying asbestos-related pleural disease. Untreated severe obstructive sleep apnea was identified as a likely contributor to orthopnea, and a trial of CPAP was well tolerated. He was started on tiotropium for COPD symptoms, and aspirin was reduced to 81 mg due to concurrent warfarin use. His INR was subtherapeutic at 1.8 at discharge, with follow-up recommended. He was discharged home with plans for sleep clinic follow-up for CPAP setup, pulmonary clinic for further respiratory evaluation, and cardiology for ICD interrogation.
